subject: Edge Pod control-plane / data-plane annotated reference & ops readout
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, infra@acme-cloud.com
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Edge Pod reference diagrams + control/data separation — kickoff

Hi all,

Following our sync last week, I attached the initial set of annotated reference diagrams for the Edge Pod private VPC that Acme will host. This version focuses on the explicit control-plane/data-plane separation we agreed on:

- Control plane (Redwood-managed APIs, cert distribution, control websocket endpoints) in a dedicated management subnet (10.100.0.0/24).
- Data plane (inference workers, KV cache proxies, inference LB) in tenant-specific data subnets (10.100.X.0/24).
- Egress choke points: NAT gateway + per-tenant egress policy enforced by Acme's egress ACLs.

Ask: please review the diagrams and confirm any missing operational acceptance criteria we should include in the runbook (esp. BGP peering expectations, KMS connectivity, and observability endpoints).

Attachments: edgepod-reference-diagrams-v1.pdf, controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx

Neha Kapoor
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Sep 4, 2026 at 09:46 AM Acme Cloud <infra@acme-cloud.com> wrote:
> Thanks Neha — attaching a TL;DR of what Acme needs (we added an egress NAT sizing note). We can host the management subnet as a separate VRF to minimize accidental cross-tenant routes.
>
> Quick clarifications:
> - Are the control-plane endpoints allowed to call back to customer KMS (ACME-KMS) or should they use Redwood-managed KMS over a designated secure tunnel?
> - For BGP: do you want full route exchange (we prefer partial with only service prefixes) or static tunnels?
>
> Will take a pass and give line-by-line comments today.
>
> — Acme Infra
From: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Edge Pod reference diagrams + control/data separation — kickoff

Thanks Neha / Acme — good kickoff. A few quick internal notes before we get into vendor-level decisions: 

1) KMS: For regulated customers we need customer-managed KMS inside their tenancy (Acme-managed HSM) for encryption-at-rest keys for model artifacts. Control-plane telemetry and runtime ephemeral keys should use a Redwood key store over a mutually-authenticated TLS tunnel (i.e., Redwood KMS via a dedicated mgmt tunnel). We should document both options in the runbook and state the trade-offs (auditability vs operational complexity).

2) BGP vs Static: Default to partial BGP (advertise service prefixes + next-hop stake) — gives us more operational visibility and faster failover. Static is fallback during initial cutover.

3) Observability: We need a separate telemetry egress for control-plane metrics (port 443 to telemetry.redwood.com) that is rate-limited and tagged. Data-plane logs should be exported to Acme's SIEM via an egress-forwarder (we will provide the fluent-bit config).

Action: Kimberly, please add KMS + telemetry acceptance criteria to the runbook draft. Marissa — could you coordinate TowerOps for the runbook playbook?

Elliot
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Adding my notes and a short checklist below; I've also uploaded a pared-down runbook template to the Drive link (see related_links).

Operational acceptance checklist (candidate):
- Control-plane connectivity: mutual TLS established between Acme mgmt subnet and Redwood control endpoints; 3 consecutive successful heartbeats in 5m window.
- KMS: ability to rotate a key and verify model artifact decrypt success within <5m.
- BGP: partial adjacency established and routes present for service prefixes; failover tested by simulating next-hop withdrawal.
- Egress accounting: per-tenant token-level cost tagging present in telemetry.
- Fail-open policy: if control-plane unreachable, data-plane must continue serving inference with read-only model cache for 30m before throttling.

Attachments referenced: controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx (contains proposed NAT sizing and per-tenant flows).

Kimberly Park
Manager, Deployment Ops
Redwood Inference
From: infra@acme-cloud.com <infra@acme-cloud.com>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 5 Sep 2026 07:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Edge Pod reference diagrams + control/data separation — kickoff

Hi team — thanks for the checklist, that helps. Responses inline: 

- KMS: We can support both models. For customer-managed KMS we will expose an internal endpoint over the VRF and can deliver an HSM-signed cert for mutual auth. For Redwood KMS we will provision a private peering and advertise only the management route. Recommend we document both in the runbook and select per-account on onboarding.

- BGP: Partial BGP preferred; we'll advertise the service blocks and withhold tenant CIDRs. We'll provide BGP community tagging so you can prefer specific paths for telemetry.

- NAT sizing: based on projected 6,000 concurrent inference workers per pod and 8k req/s egress bursts, we recommend two medium-sized NAT instances with burst autoscaling + an L4 sinkhole for traffic shaping (details in controlplane-egress-matrix.xlsx).

- Observability hooks: TowerOps will provide a pre-built fluent-bit container and a managed endpoint for SIEM ingestion. We can host a short runbook run (T+7 days) to validate pipeline.

Next steps:
1) Kimberley/Kimberly? (internal note — please standardize spelling) update the runbook template with the acceptance checklist and share to Drive.
2) Schedule a technical playbook session with TowerOps (30–40m) to walk the cutover steps. Proposed window: Tue 2026-09-08 09:00–09:40 PT.

— Acme Infra

Thanks Acme — this all looks good. Quick updates from our side after internal review: 

- We accepted partial BGP for steady-state and static for canary cutover. Add a 6-hour rollback window in the cutover runbook in case we need to revert routes.
- We'll default to Redwood KMS for the first two pilot accounts to reduce onboarding friction; include a checklist item for moving to customer-managed KMS on request.
- Observability: Marissa to own the pipeline validation with TowerOps. I'll run the T+7 validation and post the results to the Drive runbook.

Action items assigned: 
- Kimberly: update runbook + add the 6-hour rollback and fail-open thresholds (due 2026-09-09 EOD).
- Acme Infra: confirm the BGP community tags and provide the NAT autoscaling thresholds (due 2026-09-07).
- Elliot: prepare the canary acceptance prompt set and tokenized telemetry keys.

We have a tentative TowerOps technical playbook on 2026-09-08 09:00 PT — please confirm availability.

Best,

Marissa Cole
